extracted.intended_audience: general U.S. news readers / viewers of mainstream cable news
extracted.subtask_description: A news report covering a high-profile entertainer's controversial action (a gruesome photo/video) and the resulting professional and public fallout, including employer response, public figures' reactions, and the subject's apology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tastefulness / appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Anderson Cooper: 'It is clearly disgusting and completely inappropriate.' CNN said it found Griffin's actions 'disgusting and offensive.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The network and its anchors judged the image based on whether it was tasteful or appropriate for public broadcast and association; language used by CNN and Cooper frames 'tastefulness' as a core standard for continued professional association.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depiction of violence / condoning violence
rubrics_metrics.description: Griffin posted a video of herself lifting a bloodied head that appeared to resemble Trump; she wrote she doesn't condone violence and was 'merely mocking the Mocker in Chief.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether the depiction glorifies or condones violence—or is perceived as doing so—affects public and employer reaction. Denials of condoning violence are noted but may not mitigate consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional suitability for network hosting
rubrics_metrics.description: CNN has terminated our agreement with Kathy Griffin to appear on our New Year's Eve program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employers evaluate talent's public actions against standards for representatives of the network; a single controversial act can justify termination of hosting/appearance agreements regardless of past tenure (Griffin hosted since 2007).

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact on private individuals / children
rubrics_metrics.description: Trump: 'Kathy Griffin should be ashamed of herself. My children, especially my 11 year old son, Barron, are having a hard time with this. Sick!'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public figures (and their families) being affected emotionally is used as an evaluative criterion for wrongdoing or impropriety; appeals to protecting children and family feelings intensify condemnation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Context sensitivity (awareness of real-world atrocities)
rubrics_metrics.description: First lady Melania Trump: 'When you consider some of the atrocities happening in the world today, a photo opportunity like this is simply wrong and makes you wonder about the mental health of the person who did it.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actions are judged against the backdrop of ongoing real-world suffering; insensitivity to such context is framed as an additional moral failing beyond poor taste.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedic boundaries / 'crossing the line'
rubrics_metrics.description: Griffin: 'I'm a comic. I crossed the line. I move the line, then I cross it. I went way too far.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is an implicit standard for where comedic provocation becomes unacceptable; performers' own admission of having 'crossed the line' signals recognition of that boundary and factors into public assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency and timing of apology
rubrics_metrics.description: Griffin apologized in a video: 'I sincerely apologize. I'm just now seeing the reaction of these images... I went way too far.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apologies are evaluated as mitigation for harm; the article notes an apology but shows that apology may not reverse professional consequences (CNN still terminated the agreement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public/social media conduct and retraction
rubrics_metrics.description: Griffin posted tweets that were later deleted: 'Both tweets have since been deleted.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deletion of posts is noted but does not erase the circulation or consequences; social media behavior and attempts at retraction are part of how actions are judged.
